entries.evidence: Lines persist ordered model-unit endpoints (no pixel conversion); lineObjectFromPoints refuses segments shorter than 0.5 model units and the unit test proves the refusal. Length is exposed through the in-progress dimension label and driving/reference distance dimensions.
entries.gaps: No test asserts the exact (0,0)-(30,40) => 50 mm case or an angle readout on a committed line; the editor exposes endpoints, not length/direction fields.
entries.required_changes: Add a unit test for the 3-4-5 case and the committed line's length/angle readout; optionally add Length/Angle derived fields to the entity editor.
entries.acceptance: Line (0,0)-(30,40) commits with length 50 in document units; a sub-tolerance segment creates no entity and no history step.

apps/web/src/lib/sketch/session.test.ts 'rejects a zero-sweep arc instead of silently making a circle'
apps/web/src/lib/sketch/session.test.ts 'rejects arcs whose radius is below the sketch tolerance'
entries.evidence: Arcs store centre, radius and a CCW start/end angle range; only the centre-start-end construction exists. Swapping the start and end picks yields the complementary CCW arc, not the same region.
entries.gaps: Only one construction mode (no 3-point/endpoint arc, no tangent arc). No arc-length readout or test for the radius-10 semicircle (10*pi). The intended region is not preserved when endpoints are reversed, and the construction mode is not recorded.
entries.required_changes: Add 3-point (endpoint-endpoint-curvature) and tangent-from-endpoint arc modes, an arc-length readout, and a direction rule (or flip control) so reversed picks keep the intended side; add unit tests.
entries.acceptance: A radius-10 semicircle reports length 10*pi; picking its endpoints in either order with the same third point gives the same arc; each mode has unit and browser coverage.

entries.roadmap_row: none (no ROADMAP row; mentioned only in docs/reviews/reference-cad-comparison-2026-09-26.md §2.3)
code_paths: apps/web/src/lib/sketch/session.ts:1155 sketchMovePointerRole (non-owner pointers, including a stylus, are ignored mid-drag)
entries.evidence: There is no stroke-recognition path. The viewport treats pen input as an ordinary pointer and ignores a second pointer during a drag. The comparison review lists the pen-only automatic line/arc but assigns no row.
entries.gaps: Everything: stroke capture, line/arc classification, cancellation semantics.
entries.required_changes: First a product decision and a ROADMAP row; then Pointer Events (pointerType 'pen') stroke capture that resolves to an explicit line or arc object through the existing commit path, with Escape leaving no partial curve.
entries.dependencies: Product decision (no owning row); a supported pen device and human input for acceptance
entries.acceptance: With a real pen, alternating line/arc strokes resolve to line/arc objects; cancelling leaves nothing; mouse behaviour unchanged.

entries.evidence: The sketch schema, tools and region builder have no spline entity. The pinned kernel already exports interpolatePoints and makeNurbsEdge, so creating the geometry is not kernel-blocked; GCS spline entities (Remus B75) are needed only for constraints.
entries.gaps: No entity, tool, editor, region/profile support, extrude path or persistence.
entries.required_changes: Add an additive schema version with a spline objectKind (fit points plus a stated parameterisation), a region/profile path through the kernel interpolation, an editable point list, and migrations. Constraints stay on endpoints until B75 lands.
entries.dependencies: I01; Remus B75 for spline solver entities (Pinned Remus 8ef16f90 (packages/kernel-adapter/package.json:22) has interpolatePoints/makeNurbsEdge); S04 for point identity
entries.acceptance: The interpolation residual at every fit point is <=1e-9 model units; editing a fit point keeps the entity id and any endpoint constraint; save/reopen round-trips.

entries.evidence: There is no control-point (B-spline/NURBS) sketch entity or control-polygon display. The pinned kernel exposes makeNurbsEdge and getNurbsCurveData for the edge side.
entries.gaps: No degree/knots/weights representation, no control-polygon UI, no persistence.
entries.required_changes: Add a schema entity with degree, control points, a clamped knot vector and optional weights; draw the control polygon as construction; persist and migrate; feed regions through makeNurbsEdge.
entries.dependencies: I01; Remus B75 for solver support; Pinned Remus 8ef16f90 (packages/kernel-adapter/package.json:22)
entries.acceptance: Moving an interior control point keeps a clamped curve's endpoints fixed; degree and knots survive reopen bit-exactly.

tests: apps/web/src/lib/sketch/session.test.ts 'builds shapes from drags and rejects slivers'
entries.evidence: A corner-to-corner drag creates one axis-aligned parametric rectangle object that bounds a closed profile with exact area. It is a single node with no edge or corner identity, so there are no durable horizontal/vertical/coincidence relations.
entries.gaps: No durable H/V/coincident intent or corner identity (S04 is Open); no unit test for the exact (0,0)-(20,12) case with area 240 and perimeter 64.
entries.required_changes: Deliver the S04 typed corner/edge refs (or explicit decomposition to lines with constraints); add a test for area and perimeter.
entries.acceptance: Corners (0,0)/(20,12) give a closed profile with area 240 and perimeter 64; after S04, corners are constrainable and survive replay.

tests: apps/web/src/components/SketchEntityEditor.test.tsx 'keeps a rectangle construction after its width is edited'
entries.evidence: The stored model is centre-based, so numeric centre entry and width edits are symmetric with no centre drift by construction. In the viewport, however, the rectangle tool only drags corner to corner.
entries.gaps: No centre-anchored drawing mode in the viewport. No test asserts that centre (5,7) with 20x12 gives corners (-5,1)/(15,13), or that the centre stays put on resize.
entries.required_changes: Add a centre-anchored rectangle mode (strip like the circle-type strip) and a unit test for the corner/centre invariants.
entries.dependencies: S06 (drawing modes), S04 for corner identity
entries.acceptance: Centre (5,7), 20x12 gives corners (-5,1)/(15,13); a width edit keeps the centre bit-exact.

code_paths: packages/shared/src/index.ts:659-720 (SketchObjectData) rectangle has no rotation field
entries.evidence: Rectangles are axis-aligned centre/width/height objects with no rotation, and there is no three-point construction. Rotated rectangles today require four lines.

entries.acceptance: A 3-4-5 base with width 2 gives perpendicular edges and area 10; a collinear third input creates nothing.

tests: apps/web/src/lib/sketch/session.test.ts 'builds circles from opposite diameter endpoints'

entries.evidence: Circles store centre and radius, with three construction modes, unit tests and browser tests. Radius is the only stored, editable and dimensioned quantity.

entries.dependencies: S02 (reference dimensions currently cover radius only)
entries.acceptance: Radius 5 gives area 25*pi; entering diameter 12 stores radius 6 and displays the diameter label.

entries.evidence: There is no ellipse sketch entity, tool or region support. The pinned kernel already exports gcsAddEllipse/gcsSetEllipse/gcsEllipseParams and makeEllipseEdge, so the I01 note about Remus B75 does not block ellipse creation or solving.

entries.acceptance: Semi-axes 8 and 3 give area 24*pi exactly; swapping the axes with a 90 degree rotation gives the same locus.

tests: test/geometry.test.ts 'inscribes a polygon in its radius with a flat-symmetric first vertex'
entries.evidence: Regular polygons persist sides (3–64) and a circumradius, and side count is editable. They can only be created from the Inspector shape form or the AI; the viewport has no polygon tool even though the workspace hint still says 'P polygon' (App.tsx:19238).
entries.gaps: No viewport polygon tool or presets; the radius convention is labelled only 'Radius'; no test for hexagon circumradius 10 => side 10; no vertex identity (S04).

entries.acceptance: A hexagon with circumradius 10 has side 10; changing sides keeps the centre and circumradius; created from the viewport.

tests: test/text-kernel-build.test.ts ('gives counters real through-holes', 'extrudes TEXT 5 mm into one solid per letter', 'fails closed, naming the cause, when the face is not loaded')
entries.evidence: Text uses licensed bundled fonts and becomes closed contours with real counter holes; it stays parametric (string and size edits regenerate). Tests prove multi-glyph extrudes with holes. A missing face fails closed with a named warning, and missing styles fall back explicitly with no synthetic bold/italic.
entries.gaps: Text is not convertible to editable geometry (intentional). Missing-font behaviour is fail-closed rather than a substitution choice, which satisfies the 'visible decision' intent.
entries.required_changes: None required; optionally an explicit 'convert to geometry' action.
entries.acceptance: Text with counters extrudes into one solid per glyph with through-holes; an unavailable face gives a named refusal, not a silent substitute.

entries.evidence: Nothing projects model edges or other sketches into a sketch. The pinned kernel exports projectEdges and projectCurvesOntoSketchPlane, but kernel-adapter calls neither.
entries.gaps: No projection command, no linked or detached mode, no broken-reference handling.
entries.required_changes: Ship a detached-copy projection first (project edges/sketch curves to line/arc objects), then linked mode with source identity and explicit re-pick repair per I01.
entries.dependencies: I01; K05/K06 topology identity for linked mode; Pinned Remus 8ef16f90 (packages/kernel-adapter/package.json:22) has projectCurvesOntoSketchPlane
entries.acceptance: Projecting a 20x12 rectangle from a parallel plane yields a 20x12 profile; in linked mode a source width edit updates it; in detached mode it does not; deleting the source shows a named broken reference.

code_paths: apps/web/src/lib/sketch/edits.ts:529 resolveSketchLoop (refuses a non-line pick and any open run)
entries.evidence: The Offset tool takes only a closed loop of lines. A single line, an open chain, a circle or an arc is refused by name, so a single-curve offset cannot be made.
entries.gaps: No single-curve offset (line, arc or circle), no side/extension policy, no collapse refusal for circles.
entries.required_changes: Add a single-entity offset: a parallel line (with an extension policy), concentric arc/circle radius r±d, and a refusal when the radius would reach <=0.
entries.acceptance: Offsetting a radius-5 circle by +1/-1 gives radii 6/4; -5 is refused with no document change; undo is one step.

tests: packages/kernel-adapter/src/sketch-2d-ops.test.ts ('reads a straight-cornered outward offset back exactly', 'refuses an inward offset that collapses the loop', 'offsets an L profile outward')
entries.evidence: Closed line loops offset through the kernel in one undoable transaction, with coincidences closing the new loop. The adapter supports intersection (miter), arc and chamfer joins, but the UI always uses 'arc'.
entries.gaps: Join policy is not user-selectable, so the acceptance test's 22x14 sharp-corner miter result cannot be made from the UI; open chains and loops containing arcs are refused; no browser coverage of the Modify group (S05 notes this).
entries.required_changes: Expose a join choice (miter default or toggle), accept open chains and arc-containing loops, and add an e2e for the Modify group.
entries.acceptance: A 20x12 rectangle offset outward by 1 with a miter gives exactly 22x14; with the arc join, the corners are radius-1 arcs; one undo removes it.

tests: test/e2e/sketch-move.spec.ts (snapped centre drag, text ring rotate, Escape restore)
entries.evidence: One selected sketch object can be dragged (snapping, Escape restore, refusal when the drag would overwrite an expression). Only text has a rotation handle.

entries.dependencies: S03 conflict reporting; S04 for composites
entries.acceptance: Translating a three-line triangle by (10,5), rotating it 90 degrees, then applying the inverse restores its coordinates within 1e-9, with closure kept.

entries.evidence: There is no sketch-level scale. Body uniform scale exists, but nothing scales sketch entities about a pivot.
entries.gaps: Everything.
entries.required_changes: Add a selection scale about a pivot (uniform), refuse 0 or non-finite factors, and handle expression-driven fields and driving constraints explicitly (refuse or rescale).
entries.dependencies: S03 for constraint conflicts; needs a row (S05 extension)
entries.acceptance: A circle of diameter 6 scaled 1.5 has diameter 9; factor 0 is refused with no change.

entries.evidence: There is no sketch pattern tool. S05 lists linear patterns, with a persistent pattern constraint, as open.
entries.gaps: Everything, including the persistent pattern relation.
entries.required_changes: Implement count/spacing (or total) copies as one transaction, then a pattern relation that links the instances to the source until deleted.
entries.acceptance: Three circles at 12 mm spacing span 24 mm; editing the spacing moves all copies; deleting the relation leaves free copies.

entries.evidence: There is no sketch circular pattern. S05 lists circular patterns (by total or spacing, with quantity and orientation) as open.
entries.gaps: Everything.
entries.required_changes: Implement an angular pattern about an in-plane centre that separates the spacing angle from the total sweep and skips the duplicate seam instance at 360 degrees.
entries.acceptance: Four instances at 90 degree spacing fill a full turn with exactly four entities (no seam duplicate).

entries.evidence: There is no rotate-about-axis for sketch entities, and the only sketch rotation is the text ring. Off-plane results are not modelled.
entries.gaps: Everything, including the policy for off-plane results.
entries.required_changes: Define the policy first: in-plane rotation about the normal (covered by ZC-016) versus refusing out-of-plane axes or creating a new sketch support.
entries.dependencies: Design decision; R01 if a new support plane is created
entries.acceptance: Rotating an in-plane line 30 degrees about the plane normal is exact; an out-of-plane axis is refused by name or lands on a declared new sketch.

entries.evidence: There is no sketch mirror tool. The body-level mirror (command-system Mirror plane) does not apply to sketch entities. The pinned GCS has Symmetric, so persistent symmetry is app-side work (S07).
entries.gaps: Everything, including optional symmetry persistence.
entries.required_changes: Reflect the selected line/arc/circle across a picked sketch line as one transaction, keeping the source, then optionally add S07 symmetric constraints.
entries.acceptance: Reflecting (3,4) across x=0 gives (-3,4); reflecting twice gives the original coordinates; the entity count doubles per the keep-source policy.

entries.evidence: There is no trim or extend tool. S05 explicitly lists trim/extend as open; the closest app code is the crossing computation for snapping in session.ts.
entries.gaps: Everything: intersection splitting, keeping unaffected segments, reassigning or explaining dependent constraints, undo.
entries.required_changes: Implement trim on line/arc/circle using the existing exact crossings (circle becomes an arc), rewriting constraints that still apply and refusing or explaining ones that do not.
entries.acceptance: A circle crossed by a line trims only the picked arc interval; one undo restores the circle and its constraints.

code_paths: packages/document-core/src/index.ts:1469 deleteSketchObject (removes owned constraints in the same command)
entries.evidence: Delete removes the entity and its constraints as one undoable command and refuses while reference dimensions target it. It skips the checkSketchEdit downstream preflight that entity edits use (apps/web/src/lib/sketch/editing.ts:30), so the dependent-feature consequence is not shown first.
entries.gaps: No consequence preview or test showing that deleting a rectangle-profile edge leaves the dependent extrude visibly unresolved, and no test that undo restores both; delete is single-entity only.
entries.required_changes: Route delete through the downstream preflight (warn or offer, never silently break), add a regression test (profile opens, extrude reports unresolved, undo restores), and support multi-select delete.
entries.acceptance: Deleting one edge of a line rectangle opens the profile; the dependent extrude shows a named unresolved state; one undo restores the edge, constraints and extrude.

tests: test/sketch-regions.test.ts 'does not let construction geometry split or bound profiles'
apps/web/src/components/SketchEntityEditor.test.tsx 'keeps a circle construction after its radius is edited'
entries.evidence: The construction flag exists on every entity kind; the regions builder excludes construction entities, and a test proves it. The rail toggle only marks newly drawn geometry.
entries.gaps: No make-construction/make-regular action for an existing entity (the entity editor preserves the flag but cannot change it); no test that toggling one closed-loop edge removes the profile and undo restores it.
entries.required_changes: Add a construction toggle for the selected entities (one undoable updateSketchObject) and a regression test for profile loss and undo.
entries.acceptance: Toggling one edge of a closed line loop to construction removes that extrudable profile; undo restores it; the flag round-trips through save/reopen.

tests: test/kernel-conformance.test.ts:348 'solves persisted sketch constraints through the GCS' (asserts cross product < 1e-6)

entries.required_changes: None for the line case. Extend pick targets to composite edges with S04.

tests: apps/web/src/lib/sketch/constraints.test.ts:588 'solves perpendicular lines to a right angle' (|cos| < 1e-8)
entries.evidence: Perpendicular solves to a right angle against the real kernel and the degenerate collapse case is refused without publishing geometry.

entries.required_changes: Add a regression: perpendicular pair plus a driving length, change the length, re-solve, assert dot product ~0 and the length.
entries.acceptance: Dot product of normalized directions < 1e-8 after the initial solve and after a driving-length edit.

entries.roadmap_row: S07 (constraint set); S05 for fillet-written arc tangency

Circle-circle tangency has no native kernel constraint (emulate via centre distance).

tests: apps/web/src/lib/sketch/edits.test.ts:337 'survives a driving-dimension change on either source line' (fillet coincidences hold after a driver edit)
entries.evidence: Point-point coincidence (line/arc endpoints, circle centres) is authorable and maps to kernel `coincident`; the fillet driver-change test shows joined endpoints follow a driving edit.
entries.gaps: No point-on-curve intent (point on line/circle/arc) even though the kernel has pointOnCircle/pointOnArc/pointLineDistance; no drop-a-point-on-a-point creation (S07); no direct line-line endpoint residual oracle under a drag.
entries.required_changes: Add point-on-curve coincidence variants to the schema and tool; add drag-onto-point creation (S07); add a plain two-line coincident + driver-edit residual test.
entries.dependencies: Remus pin 8ef16f90 (packages/kernel-adapter/package.json) already parses symmetric, symmetricAboutPoint, fixX, fixY, pointLineDistance, pointOnCircle, pointOnArc, tangentArcArc, arcLength (crates/wasm/src/bindings/gcs_sketch.rs:140-249); gcsAddPoint takes a fixed flag.
entries.acceptance: Joined endpoints stay within 1e-9 after a driving edit; a point constrained onto a line/circle stays on it after the driver moves.

tests: apps/web/src/lib/sketch/constraints.test.ts:662 'solves a point onto another lines midpoint'
entries.evidence: A snap point can be bound to a line's midpoint and the solve oracle checks the point lands on ((x1+x2)/2,(y1+y2)/2).

entries.evidence: Circle/arc concentricity is authorable (circle-circle mapped to coincident centres, arcs to concentricArc*), and the oracle asserts a shared centre.

entries.evidence: Horizontal is stored in sketch-local coordinates and solved by the kernel; the conformance test asserts equal endpoint y. Camera orientation never enters the solve input, so view rotation cannot redefine it.
